abstain

/ab-STAYN/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Abstain means to freely choose not to do something, especially through self-restraint.

During training season the sprinter abstained from sugary drinks entirely.

Example

Every winter, Amir's family hosted a legendary dessert table: three pies, a chocolate fountain, his aunt's caramel bars. This year Amir had promised his dentist a clean checkup after two rough visits. He filled his plate with fruit, poured himself tea, and sat at the far end of the table. When the caramel bars came around for the third time, he passed the tray along without taking one. Choosing restraint when no one would have blamed him for indulging — that is what it means to abstain.

Amir freely passes up desserts he loves, out of deliberate self-restraint rather than outside pressure, which is exactly what abstaining is.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

refrain: Refrain means to stop yourself from doing a particular thing, usually briefly and in the moment - you refrain from interrupting. Abstain is self-denial with commitment behind it: freely giving up something you enjoy, often for a long stretch and for a reason like health or principle. You refrain from a remark; you abstain from caffeine for a month.

forgo: Forgo means to go without something, to give it up or do without - and it says nothing about why. You might forgo dessert simply because the line is too long. Abstain makes the reason part of the meaning: a free, deliberate act of self-restraint. Forgoing is the going-without; abstaining is the disciplined choice behind it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

indulge: to give in to a desire

partake: to take part; to have some

Where it sits · how deliberate and lasting the refusal is — skip → abstain → renounce

skip vs. abstain: Skip is casual and weaker — you might skip dessert once without a second thought; to abstain is to hold yourself back deliberately, usually as a sustained act of self-restraint.

renounce vs. abstain: Renounce is stronger than abstain: renouncing something means formally giving it up forever, not just choosing restraint for now.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — abs-

Prefix — abs-: away from

Root — tain

Root — tain: to hold (Latin tenere)

Put it together

Put it together: Abstain comes from Latin abstinere: abs- (away) plus tenere (to hold). To abstain is literally to hold yourself away from something. The same tenere runs through retain (hold back), contain (hold together), and maintain (hold in hand) — a whole family of English words about holding.

Use the root in a new word: retain

Use the root in a new word: retain: Despite three changes of ownership, the restaurant has managed to retain its original head chef.

Word Choice

neutral-to-formal; health, ethics, and voting contexts

Abstain takes 'from' ('abstain from soda') and always implies a free choice — if allergies or rules stop you, you are not abstaining. In parliamentary settings it has the special sense of declining to vote either way.
